59	    /// Re-copies the bundled statusline.sh over the installed one if they
60	    /// differ, but ONLY if the HUD is already installed — never installs it
61	    /// for someone who hasn't opted in. Without this, `install()` only ever
62	    /// runs once (when the user clicks "Turn on HUD"), so every fix or
63	    /// field added to statusline.sh since then — the null-vs-0 handling and
64	    /// claudePid/fleetPaneId fields, for one — silently never reached an
65	    /// existing install. Cheap (one byte comparison); call it once at
66	    /// startup, not on a timer.
67	    @discardableResult
68	    static func upgradeIfStale() -> Bool {
69	        guard isInstalled, let src = bundledScript,
70	              FileManager.default.fileExists(atPath: installedScript.path) else { return false }
71	        guard let newData = try? Data(contentsOf: src),
72	              let oldData = try? Data(contentsOf: installedScript),
73	              newData != oldData else { return false }
74	        do {
75	            try FileManager.default.removeItem(at: installedScript)
76	            try FileManager.default.copyItem(at: src, to: installedScript)
77	            try FileManager.default.setAttributes([.posixPermissions: 0o755], ofItemAtPath: installedScript.path)
78	            return true
79	        } catch { return false }
80	    }

82	    /// Wires the HUD into an extra account's own settings.json (Claude Code
83	    /// reads settings from $CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, not ~/.claude, when it's
84	    /// set). Uses the same installed script; no previous-statusLine
85	    /// bookkeeping — an account folder fleet created has nothing to restore.
86	    static func install(claudeConfigDir dir: URL) {
87	        // Only ever copies the script — never falls back to install(), which
88	        // would also rewrite the DEFAULT ~/.claude/settings.json as a side
89	        // effect of adding an account.
90	        guard FileManager.default.fileExists(atPath: installedScript.path) || copyScript() else { return }
91	        let url = dir.appendingPathComponent("settings.json")
92	        var settings = readJSON(url) ?? [:]
93	        settings["statusLine"] = ["type": "command", "command": installedScript.path, "padding": 0]
94	        writeJSON(url, settings)
95	    }
